findings.title: deleteCache handler throws a plain Error and only authorizes user-owned credentials
findings.body: The handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of a `TRPCError`. tRPC maps unknown errors to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so an authorization failure is reported to the client as a 500 and logged/alerted as a server bug rather than a 403/404. Additionally, the authorization check is `where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }`, so credentials owned by a team (`userId` is null, `teamId` set) can never be matched; the UI will still render the "Delete cached data" action for such a credential and the user gets an opaque server error. Use `TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN" | "NOT_FOUND" })` and include the team-admin case in the access check (or hide the action for team credentials).

findings.title: Cache deletion never invalidates the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), nothing invalidates the query that provides `cacheUpdatedAt`. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` the prop is wired to `props.onChanged`, which is optional and not supplied on the installed-apps page, and the query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. Consequence: after a successful delete the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated: …" timestamp and the "Delete cached data" entry until a full reload, making it look as if the deletion failed. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` to the mutation's settled/success handler.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to the en-US locale and ignores the user's time format
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` formats the cache timestamp with a fixed US locale, so non-US users see MM/DD/YY and a 12-hour clock regardless of their configured locale/`timeFormat` (24h) preference. The surrounding string is translated via `t("cache_last_updated")`, which makes the mix of translated label and US-formatted date inconsistent. Use the active i18n locale (e.g. `i18n.language`) and the user's time-format preference, or the existing dayjs/date formatting helpers used elsewhere in the app.

findings.title: Confirm buttons are not disabled while mutations are in flight and errors lose server detail
findings.body: `onConfirm` fires `deleteCacheMutation.mutate` / `disconnectMutation.mutate` and immediately closes the dialog without any pending/disabled state, so a user can re-open and re-trigger the mutation while the first request is still running. Also both `onError` handlers discard `error.message` and show a generic toast, so real failures (e.g. the "Credential not found or access denied" case from `deleteCache.handler.ts`) are indistinguishable from transient errors, making support/debugging harder. Wire `isPending` to the dialog's confirm button and surface the server message in the error toast.

findings.title: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache relies on an empty updateMany payload to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object and depends entirely on Prisma implicitly injecting the `@updatedAt` field into the generated UPDATE. That is non-obvious and fragile (if Prisma treats the empty payload as a no-op the intended timestamp bump silently never happens), and the intent is not verifiable from the code. It also runs on every cache fill — an extra write per credential in the cache-warming cron path — for a field that nothing in this PR reads (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`). Either pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly or drop the call. Note that for in-memory delegation credentials `this.credential.id` is negative, so the update matches no rows at all.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId is typed with UpdateInput but calls updateMany
findings.body: The new method accepts `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` but forwards it to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`, which requires `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`. `UpdateInput` permits nested relation operations (e.g. `user: { connect: { id } }`, `credential: { disconnect: true }`) that `updateMany` cannot execute, so such a call type-checks but fails at runtime with a Prisma validation error. Change the parameter type to `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId that nothing in this PR consumes
findings.body: `UserWithCalendars.allSelectedCalendars` / `userLevelSelectedCalendars` were widened from `Pick<SelectedCalendar, "externalId" | "integration" | "eventTypeId">` to also require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. This is a breaking contract change for every caller that builds this object from a narrower Prisma `select` (platform API v2 / `@calcom/platform-libraries` consumers of `getConnectedDestinationCalendars`), which will now fail type-check and need matching select changes. Neither field is used by the cache-status feature added here (the handler reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`), and adding them to `findUnlockedUserForSession`'s select also enlarges the session payload for no benefit. Revert the type widening unless there is a consumer.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt and reports expired cache as present
findings.body: The `groupBy` only filters on `credentialId`, so rows whose `expiresAt` is already in the past are included in the max-`updatedAt` result. `getCachedAvailability` refuses to serve those rows (`expiresAt: { gte: now }`), so the UI will show a "Cache Status / Last updated …" entry and offer "Delete cached data" for a credential whose cache can no longer be used — a misleading status for a diagnostics feature. Filter by `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or surface expiry separately).

findings.title: connectedCalendars always runs an extra cache groupBy and bypasses the CalendarCache feature-flag factory
findings.body: The handler instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init`, so the `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` (used when calendar-cache is disabled) is bypassed and an additional `calendarCache.groupBy` query is executed on every call to this frequently-used endpoint, even for users/teams that have the calendar-cache feature off. Either skip the query when the feature is disabled or short-circuit when `credentialIds` is empty, and go through the existing factory so the enabled/disabled behaviour is consistent with the rest of the calendar-cache code.

findings.title: Migration header warning contradicts the SQL it documents
findings.body: The generated warning block states "Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.", but the statement below adds the column `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`, which is safe for a non-empty table. Leaving the stale warning in place makes reviewers/operators believe this migration will fail or needs a manual backfill. Remove or correct the comment block.

findings.title: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's CWD and can write a .env outside the repo
findings.body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current working directory, not to the script location. Running the script the obvious way from the repository root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) resolves to `<parent-of-checkout>/.env`: the script happily creates that file (`touch "$ENV_FILE"`) and writes `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` into it, polluting a directory outside the repo while the developer's real `.env` is never updated — so the webhook test silently does not work. Resolve the path from the script directory (e.g. `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/.env"`).

findings.title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and breaks on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD form where `-i` takes a separate (empty) backup suffix. With GNU sed (Linux, CI containers) `-i` does not consume the next argument, so `''` is parsed as the sed script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, causing the command to fail and the env file to be left unmodified. Use a portable approach (e.g. write to a temp file and `mv`, or detect the sed flavour).

findings.title: cleanup() always exits 0, so failures report success
findings.body: `cleanup()` ends with `exit 0` and is used both as the SIGINT/SIGTERM trap and as the failure path for "Rate limit hit" (line 49) and "Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL" (line 58). The script therefore terminates with status 0 even when it never obtained a tunnel URL and never configured `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`, so any wrapper script or CI step cannot detect the failure. Use a non-zero exit code for the error paths.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` without adding tsx as a dependency
findings.body: `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` relies on `npx` fetching `tsx` from the network at run time; the package is not in `dependencies`/`devDependencies`, so the version is unpinned and unaffected by the lockfile, and the command fails in offline/sandboxed environments. Meanwhile `ts-node` is still a devDependency and is still used by the sibling scripts (`check-changed-files`, `translate-locales`), so the toolchain is now inconsistent. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or revert to `ts-node`.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache authorization or cache-status aggregation
findings.body: This PR adds a destructive mutation (`viewer.calendars.deleteCache`) whose only protection is an ownership lookup, plus a new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregation and the credential→cache mapping in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, and none of them have unit tests. At minimum there should be tests asserting that (a) deleting cache for a credential belonging to another user is rejected, (b) a successful call removes only the rows for that credentialId, and (c) `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returns the latest `updatedAt` per credential and maps correctly to `cacheUpdatedAt` (including the no-cache case).
